name: Berwick
note: Only in 1879, first on the list before Longstone; probably the Berwick pier light.

name: Inner Farne
note: 'Farn Islands' (1879) sits in the Inner Farne slot between Longstone and Coquet Island, so it is taken to be Inner Farne.

name: Tees No. 5 Buoy L.V.
note: 'Teesmouth' (Lightvessel, No. 5 Buoy), 'No. 5 Buoy, Teesmouth', 'Tees' L.V. and '5 Buoy Tees' are all one vessel. In 1883 and 1884 it is printed ahead of Coquet Island.

name: Teesmouth (second 1880 entry)
note: 1880 only, no. 44b, printed right after the Teesmouth light-vessel (44a). It has no type and it is not the vessel. It may be a shore light at the Tees mouth. It cannot be South Gare, which was not lit until 1884. Kind unknown.

name: South Gare (Tees Breakwater)
note: 'Tees Breakwater' L.H., 1885-86.

name: Spurn Point
note: 'Spurn' printed as L.H. (1882-87) is the lighthouse; it is printed just before the Spurn L.V.

name: Spurn (Newsand) L.V.
note: 'Spurn' Lightvessel, 6 miles S.S.E. of Spurn Point, is the same vessel as 'Spurn (Newsand)'.

name: Bull L.V.
note: 1879 only, mouth of Humber.

name: Great Cotes
note: 1880 only, no. 48b, with no type. It takes the Bull L.V.'s 1879 place between the Spurn vessel and Outer Dowsing. It might be the Bull vessel under a shore address (Great Coates is near Grimsby), or it might be a Humber shore light. Kept separate; please check.

name: Lynn Well L.V.
note: 'Llyn Wells' (1882-87) is a misspelling of Lynn Well.

name: Northrepps
note: 1880 only, no. 55a, printed between Cromer and Leman and Ower (55b), with no type. It is not Cromer, which is a separate row (54) in the same list. Kind and identity unknown.

name: Leman and Ower L.V.
note: Printed 'L.H.' in 1887, which is a slip: it is still between Winterton and Newarp.

name: Happisburgh
note: Hasborough, Hasbrough or Hasbro' printed as L.H. or Lighthouse. Kept apart from the light-vessel by the printed type.

name: Happisburgh L.V.
note: Hasborough, Hasbrough or Hasbro' printed as L.V. or Lightvessel ('north end Hasborough Sound').

name: Landguard Point
note: Printed 'Languard'.

name: North Sand Head (Goodwin) L.V.
note: 'Goodwin' L.V. and 'North Sand Head' L.V. never appear in the same list. Both come between North Foreland and the Gull, and in the 1885 and 1887 master lists North Sand Head has no. 60, Goodwin's place. So they are taken to be one vessel, the North Sand Head of the Goodwins. Please check.

name: Heligoland
note: Printed in the 1880 English east list and in the outlying section of the master lists.
edits: Gätke's island station: the observer was not a light-keeper.

name: Allonby
note: 1881 only, no. 121, first on the west coast list, printed as L.H. There is no well-known Allonby lighthouse, so it may be a nearby Solway light under a village name. Please check.
edits: Printed 'Allonby, L.H.' once (1881, no. 121) with C. Donald Thompson, who in 1887 is a private observer at Seaton-Carew; checked against Findlay below.

name: Dee L.V.
note: 'River Dee' in 1886-87.

name: Point of Ayr (Flintshire)
note: Printed 'Air'. This is the Dee estuary light, not Point of Ayre in the Isle of Man.

name: Skerries
note: 'Skerries Rock' in 1886-87.

name: North Stack
note: Printed as L.H. in 1880 and as 'Fog Horn Station' in 1881. North Stack was a fog signal station.

name: St Tudwal's
note: 'St. Judwall' (1880, no. 118, between South Stack and Caernarvon Bay) is a misprint.

name: St Ann's Head Low (Milford Low)
note: 1880-81, its own row.

name: St Ann's Head High (Milford High)
note: 1880-81, its own row.

name: St Ann's Head (Milford), single row
note: From 1884 on, 'Milford' (no. 136) and in 1886-87 'Milford (St Ann's)' take the place of the two Milford rows. The list does not say which light this row is, so it is kept apart. If the returns show which light it is, merge it into st-anns-head-high or st-anns-head-low.

name: Nash Point Low (West)
note: Own row in 1880-81.

name: Nash Point High (East)
note: From 1884 only 'Nash (E.)' is printed, as no. 140. The plain 'Nash' row in the master lists has the same number, so it is put here.

name: Breaksea L.V.
note: Printed 'L.H.' in 1884-85, which is a slip. The other years print it as L.V.

name: West Usk
edits: The lists' 'Usk L.H.': East Usk lighthouse was built in 1893, so in 1879-87 the Usk light is West Usk (run 2's reading).

name: Avonmouth (Avon)
note: Printed 'Avon, E. of entrance'.

name: Lundy Fog Gun Station
note: Its own row next to the Lundy light (1880 no. 139, 1881 no. 151).

name: St Agnes (Scilly)
note: Printed 'Scilly', St Agnes.

name: Bahama Bank L.V.
note: 'Bahama Rock' (1882) is a misprint.

name: Langness
note: 'Longness' L.V. (1882, no. 120, last after Bahama Rock) is Langness. The spelling and the L.V. type are slips, probably carried down from the Bahama row above.

name: Ballinacourty (Dungarvan)
note: Printed 'Dungarvan'. Taken to be the Ballinacourty Point light.

name: Tuskar Rock
note: The 1883 'Lt.-ship' type is a ditto slip from Barrels Rock.

name: Kish Bank L.V.
note: 'Kirk Bank' (1881, no. 10, between Arklow S. and Howth Baily) is a misprint.

name: Copeland / Mew Island
note: The Copeland light moved from Lighthouse Island to Mew Island in 1884, hence 'Copeland (Mew) Island' in 1885-86. The station keeps its number 13 throughout, so all forms are put together. Split them if you want the two towers apart.

name: Maidens North
note: Until 1886 there is one 'Maidens' row, no. 14. In 1887 the list has 'Maidens, North' (14) and 'Maidens, South' (14*). The plain row goes with North because it has the same number; the starred number marks the added row. It may in fact stand for the pair. Please check.

name: Maidens South
note: Only in 1887, no. 14*.

name: Fanad Head (Lough Swilly)
note: Printed 'Lough Swilly'. Taken to be Fanad Head, the Lough Swilly entrance light. Please check.

name: Rotten Island (Killybegs)
note: Printed 'Killybegs'. Taken to be the Rotten Island harbour light. Please check.
edits: Both runs: the lists' 'Killybegs' is the light at the harbour entrance.

name: Oyster Island
note: 'Oyster Island N.' appears twice for 1881 (two readings, both no. 23). Merged.

name: Eeragh (Aran North)
note: 'Arran Island, Is.' (1887, no. 32, between Slyne Head S. and Arran Island S.) is a misprint for 'N.'

name: Inisheer (Aran South)
note: 'Straw Island, S.' (1882, no. 34, between Straw Island and Loop Head) is a misprint. No. 34 is Aran South's number in every year, and 1882 has no other Aran South row.

name: Calf Rock
note: Only in 1881, no. 40. The tower was wrecked in November 1881.

name: Dursey Island
note: From 1882, no. 40, in Calf Rock's place. This is probably the replacement light on Dursey for the wrecked Calf Rock. It is kept separate because it is a different light at a different place; merge it with calf-rock if you want the station's run unbroken.

name: Iceland
note: Master lists only, no. 1. Possibly Reykjanes, Iceland's only lighthouse then, but it may be an observer. Kind unknown.

name: Iceland (second station, 'Do.')
note: 'Do.' under Iceland, no. 2, is a second Iceland station. Its place is not named; check the reports.

name: Faroe
note: Faroe had no lighthouse before 1893, so this is presumably an observer. Kind unknown.

name: Malmö
note: Kind assumed from the name; check.

name: Muckle Flugga (North Unst)
note: 'North Uist' (1881-82, Shetland, no. 4, first on the list) is a misprint for North Unst.

name: Bressay
note: Also printed 'Bressay Sound'.

name: Fair Isle
note: Numbered 7B (1881-83) and 3b (master lists). Fair Isle had no lighthouse until 1892, so this is an observer. Kind is 'other'.

name: Hoy High (Hoy Sound High)
note: The 1879 ditto line '"     (High)' under Hoy Sound (Low).

name: Tarbat Ness
note: Also printed 'Tarbat Head' (1885) and 'Tarbet Ness'.

name: Scurdie Ness (Montrose)
note: Printed 'Montroseness'.

name: North Carr L.V.
note: Printed 'Carr Rock', Light-ship, no. 26B.

name: Arnish Point (Stornoway)
note: 'Stornoway (2 Lights)' in 1887 is a single row, so it is one station.

name: Eilean Glas
note: Printed 'Island Glass', 'Island Ghlais' and 'Island of Ghlais'.

name: Rona (South Rona)
note: 'Bona' (1881, no. 89, between Barra Head and Kyleakin) is a misprint. Rona itself is missing from 1881.

name: Hynish Signal Tower
note: The Skerryvore shore station on Tiree. It has its own row (no. 93) in 1879-84, next to Skerryvore.

name: Skerryvore
note: In 1885-87 the two rows are joined as 'Skerryvore and Hynish Signal Tower' (no. 93). The joined row is put with the light, but it stands for both stations. Split it out if you prefer.

name: Rubha nan Gall (Sound of Mull)
note: Printed 'Sound of Mull', Tobermory.

name: Corran Point (Corran Ferry)
note: 'Conan Ferry' (1881, Loch Eil, no. 97) is a misprint.

name: Rhinns of Islay
note: 'Rhinns of May' (1887 master list, no. 102, between Skervuile and Lochindaul) is a misprint.

name: Holy Isle (Lamlash)
note: Printed 'Lamlash', Arran. Taken to be the Holy Isle light at Lamlash, lit 1877. Please check.
